_meta.source: Articles 4, 16, 25, 26, 27 and Chapter III Sections 2 and 3, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
_meta.note: Deployer obligations are the toolkit's focus. Provider obligations are summarised at chapter level only; a deployer that rebrands, substantially modifies, or repurposes a system into high-risk use becomes a provider under Article 25.

high_risk_deployer.summary: Take appropriate technical and organisational measures to use the system in accordance with its instructions for use
Assign human oversight to natural persons with the necessary competence, training, authority and support
To the extent the deployer controls input data, ensure it is relevant and sufficiently representative for the intended purpose
Monitor operation per the instructions for use; inform the provider and authorities of risks or serious incidents and suspend use where indicated

Keep automatically generated logs under the deployer's control for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, at least six months unless applicable Union or national law, in particular on the protection of personal data, provides otherwise
Before putting a workplace high-risk system into service or using it, deployers who are employers inform workers' representatives and the affected workers

Inform natural persons that they are subject to the use of a high-risk Annex III system that makes or assists decisions relating to them; for systems used for law enforcement purposes, Article 13 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 applies instead

Fundamental rights impact assessment before first use, for public-law bodies, private entities providing public services, and deployers of credit-scoring and life/health insurance pricing systems (Annex III 5(b) and 5(c)); systems intended for the critical-infrastructure area (Annex III point 2) are excepted

high_risk_provider_summary.article: Arts. 8-15 (Chapter III Section 2), the provider obligations within Section 3 (Arts. 16-22), and Arts. 43, 49 and 72
high_risk_provider_summary.summary: Risk management system (Art. 9), data governance (Art. 10), technical documentation (Art. 11), record-keeping (Art. 12), transparency to deployers (Art. 13), human oversight design (Art. 14), accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity (Art. 15), quality management, conformity assessment, registration and post-market monitoring

triggers: Putting your name or trademark on a high-risk system already on the market
Making a substantial modification to a high-risk system that keeps it high-risk
Modifying the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system so it becomes high-risk

ai_literacy.summary: Take measures to support the development of AI literacy among staff and other persons dealing with AI systems on the organisation's behalf (wording per the Digital Omnibus, signed 8 July 2026, not yet in force; until then the binding Article 4 text requires measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy)
